uncited: The method voxelize the input SfM points to create anchors.

It represents a modification of existing 2D-GS [15] and 3D-GS [5] techniques to incorporate an anchor-based organization, building on the concepts explored in Scaffold-GS [3] regarding anchor-based representations.

The specific layout of the Gaussian attributes (position, covariance, opacity, color) follows the standard definitions of the parent method (2D-GS or 3D-GS), but their spatial distribution is constrained by the anchor grid [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the authors modified 2D-GS and 3D-GS to create 'Anchor-2D-GS' and 'Anchor-3D-GS' by voxelizeing input points to anchors and assigning Gaussians to them. It confirms that these modified versions maintain the same densification strategy (implying the standard Gaussian attributes and layout definitions are preserved) but are organized by an anchor grid structure. The evidence further notes that this anchor design organizes primitives more efficiently, reducing redundancy, which supports the claim that the spatial distribution is constrained by the anchor grid.
